topic: Current news topic: the tension between AI regulation and the AI race. On one side, governments, regulators, and international bodies are pushing new AI safety rules, oversight requirements, and governance frameworks. On the other side, major AI companies and competing nations continue to race intensely to build and deploy more powerful AI systems faster than rivals. Aim: cover this tension between AI safety/regulation efforts and the competitive AI race as a current-events news story, using only facts confirmed by web search (no invented details, no facts supplied from the assistant's own prior knowledge).

kept_facts.claim: From 2 August 2026, the European Commission’s AI Office and national authorities began enforcing applicable provisions of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, including rules on prohibited AI practices, certain transparency obligations, and general-purpose AI models. ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/commission-starts-enforcing-ai-act-rules-and-new-transparency-requirements-2-august))
kept_facts.subject: European Union AI Act enforcement
kept_facts.scope: Providers and deployers subject to the EU AI Act; prohibited practices, specified transparency duties, and GPAI-model obligations
kept_facts.conditions: Some systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 receive until 2 December 2026 to comply with certain marking and detection duties.
kept_facts.numeric_scope: Enforcement start date and transitional compliance date
kept_facts.source_title: Commission starts enforcing AI Act rules and new transparency requirements on 2 August
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Do not imply that every EU AI Act obligation became enforceable on 2 August 2026; different provisions have different application dates.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 主張の中心部分は確認できる。欧州委員会のAI Officeと各国当局は2026年8月2日から、禁止行為、一定の透明性義務、GPAI規則を含む該当するAI Act規定の執行を開始した。市場投入済みシステムのArticle 50(2)のマーキング・検出義務には2026年12月2日までの経過措置がある。なお、AI Officeの執行権限は全システムに一律に及ぶわけではない。 ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/commission-starts-enforcing-ai-act-rules-and-new-transparency-requirements-2-august))

kept_facts.claim: Under the EU AI Act, obligations for all providers of general-purpose AI models entered into application on 2 August 2025. The obligations include technical documentation, a copyright policy, and a public summary of training content. Providers of GPAI models with systemic risk also face duties involving Commission notification, risk assessment and mitigation, incident reporting, and cybersecurity protections. ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/general-purpose-ai-obligations-under-ai-act))
kept_facts.subject: EU general-purpose AI obligations
kept_facts.scope: Providers of general-purpose AI models; additional duties apply to providers of GPAI models with systemic risk
kept_facts.conditions: The systemic-risk obligations apply only to models classified as posing systemic risk under the AI Act.
kept_facts.source_title: General-purpose AI obligations under the AI Act
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Distinguish mandatory legal obligations from the voluntary Code of Practice used as a compliance tool.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 2025年8月2日からGPAI提供者向け義務が適用され、技術文書、著作権方針、訓練内容の公開要約、さらにシステミックリスクGPAIについて通知、リスク評価・軽減、インシデント報告、サイバーセキュリティ保護が求められることは直接確認できる。なお、2025年8月2日以前に市場投入されたモデルには2027年8月2日までの遵守期限があるため、「全提供者が同日に直ちに遵守済み」とは書かない方がよい。 ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/general-purpose-ai-obligations-under-ai-act))

kept_facts.claim: European Commission guidance states that models trained with more than 10^23 floating-point operations and capable of generating language are considered general-purpose AI models; models trained with more than 10^25 floating-point operations are presumed to pose systemic risk, although that threshold is under review. ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/general-purpose-ai-obligations-under-ai-act))
kept_facts.subject: EU AI Act GPAI classification thresholds
kept_facts.date_or_period: Guidance current as of the source update
kept_facts.scope: Models assessed under the EU AI Act’s GPAI and systemic-risk provisions
kept_facts.conditions: The 10^25-FLOP systemic-risk threshold is expressly identified as under review.
kept_facts.numeric_scope: GPAI classification and systemic-risk presumption thresholds
kept_facts.source_title: General-purpose AI obligations under the AI Act
kept_facts.ambiguity: The systemic-risk threshold may change because the Commission states that it is under review.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Do not present the 10^25-FLOP threshold as permanently fixed.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 欧州委員会のページは、10^23 FLOP超で言語生成能力を持つモデルをGPAIとして扱い、10^25 FLOP超のモデルをシステミックリスクと推定すると記載している。また、10^25 FLOPの閾値は現在見直し中と明記されている。 ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/general-purpose-ai-obligations-under-ai-act))

kept_facts.claim: The United Nations General Assembly established an Independent International Scientific Panel on AI through Resolution A/RES/79/325 on 26 August 2025. The panel has 40 members, produces annual scientific assessments, and is not a regulatory or enforcement body; its work is non-prescriptive and does not itself create binding international AI regulation. ([un.org](https://www.un.org/independent-international-scientific-panel-ai/en?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.subject: United Nations AI governance mechanisms
kept_facts.scope: UN member states and stakeholders receiving the panel’s assessments
kept_facts.conditions: The panel informs international governance discussions but does not set or enforce rules.
kept_facts.source_title: FAQ | Independent International Scientific Panel on AI
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Do not describe the UN panel as an international regulator or as having authority to impose binding rules.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 国連総会決議79/325による2025年8月26日の設立、40人の構成員、年次評価の役割は確認できる。国連FAQも、同パネルは規制・執行機関ではなく、規則制定、基準執行、政策の強制を行わない非規範的な分析機関で、活動自体が拘束的な国際AI規制を作るものではないと明記している。 ([un.org](https://www.un.org/independent-international-scientific-panel-ai/en?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: The UN Independent International Scientific Panel on AI’s preliminary report, released in July 2026, identified as a central warning that current safeguards cannot keep pace with the growth of AI capabilities. ([un.org](https://www.un.org/independent-international-scientific-panel-ai/en/preliminary-report?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.subject: International assessment of AI safeguards
kept_facts.scope: Global assessment of AI capabilities, risks, impacts, and governance
kept_facts.conditions: This is the panel’s assessment in a preliminary report, not a legally binding determination.
kept_facts.source_title: Preliminary Report | Independent International Scientific Panel on AI
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Attribute the safeguard-gap assessment to the UN panel; do not convert it into an independently proven causal claim.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 予備報告書は2026年7月1日に公開され、中心的警告として、現在の安全策がAI能力の成長に追いついていないと記載している。これはパネルの評価として提示されたものであり、法的判断や独立に実証された因果関係ではないというFactの限定も妥当。 ([un.org](https://www.un.org/independent-international-scientific-panel-ai/en/preliminary-report?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: In its cyber evaluations, AISI reported that the best AI models completed apprentice-level tasks 50% of the time on average, compared with just over 10% in early 2024; it also reported that the length of cyber tasks models could complete without human direction was doubling roughly every eight months. AISI separately reported finding vulnerabilities in every system it tested, while safeguard progress varied across models and misuse categories. ([aisi.gov.uk](https://www.aisi.gov.uk/frontier-ai-trends-report))
kept_facts.subject: AI capability and safeguard trends in AISI testing
kept_facts.scope: AISI’s cyber evaluations and tested model safeguards
kept_facts.conditions: The figures are evaluation results, not measurements of all real-world AI deployments; the report notes uncertainty and variation by model and task.
kept_facts.numeric_value: 50%; just over 10%; approximately eight months; every tested system
kept_facts.numeric_scope: Average task success, historical comparison, estimated capability doubling interval, and tested-system vulnerability finding
kept_facts.ambiguity: The eight-month figure is described as an estimated upper bound, and the testing does not establish that capability growth caused a particular real-world harm.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Do not state that capability growth automatically produces misuse or that safeguards universally deteriorated.
kept_facts.verification_notes: AISIは、最良のモデルが見習いレベルのサイバー課題を平均50%の確率で完了し、2024年初頭の10%強から上昇したと報告している。また、モデルが人間の指示なしに完了できるサイバー課題の長さはおよそ8か月ごとに倍増する推定上限とされる。全テスト対象システムでユニバーサル・ jailbreakを発見したこと、モデル・悪用カテゴリーごとに安全策の進展が不均一であることも記載されている。 ([aisi.gov.uk](https://www.aisi.gov.uk/frontier-ai-trends-report?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: OpenAI reported that it held back larger reinforcement-learning runs for future versions of its Astra model while establishing higher safety and security requirements for the training environment. It said the large frontier reinforcement-learning run was restarted on 28 August 2026, while some smaller experimental runs remained temporarily held back. ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/path-to-astra/))
kept_facts.subject: OpenAI Astra development and safety controls
kept_facts.scope: OpenAI’s internal Astra training and development process
kept_facts.conditions: The account is OpenAI’s own description of its development decisions and does not independently establish the effectiveness of the safeguards.
kept_facts.numeric_scope: Date on which OpenAI said the large frontier reinforcement-learning run was restarted
kept_facts.source_title: Path to Astra: critical capabilities and frontier safeguards
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Do not infer that the pause fully stopped Astra development or that it proves safety was achieved.
kept_facts.verification_notes: OpenAIの2026年9月1日の説明は、将来版Astra向けの大規模RL実行を一時保留し、訓練環境の安全・セキュリティ要件を引き上げたこと、2026年8月28日に大規模フロンティアRL実行を再開したこと、なお一部の小規模実験的実行を保留していることを明記している。効果が実証された、またはAstra開発全体が停止したという含意はない。 ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/path-to-astra/))

kept_facts.claim: On 9 September 2026, OpenAI called for mandatory, capability-based national AI safety regulation in the United States. Its proposed framework includes common testing and independent-assessment requirements, stronger cybersecurity protections, incident-reporting rules, national preparedness, and measures tracking progress toward recursive self-improvement. OpenAI stated that safety should take priority if meeting safety thresholds requires slowing capability growth. ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/ai-policy-window/))
kept_facts.subject: OpenAI policy position on federal AI regulation
kept_facts.scope: OpenAI’s policy advocacy in the United States; proposed national framework
kept_facts.conditions: These are OpenAI policy positions and proposals, not enacted federal law.
kept_facts.numeric_scope: Publication date of OpenAI’s policy statement
kept_facts.source_title: The AI policy window is open. We need to act.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Attribute the proposals to OpenAI; do not describe them as government requirements or as evidence that all AI companies share the same position.
kept_facts.verification_notes: OpenAIは2026年9月9日、議会とともに義務的・能力ベースの全国AI安全規制を進めたいと表明した。提案枠組みには共通テスト、独立評価、サイバーセキュリティ、インシデント報告、国家的備え、再帰的自己改善に向けた進展の測定が含まれる。また、安全基準を満たすために能力向上を遅らせる必要がある場合は安全を優先すると述べている。いずれもOpenAIの政策提案であり、成立法ではない。 ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/ai-policy-window/?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: Anthropic stated that, within a company, “pacing” the frontier means making decisions that prioritize safety over speed when the two conflict. It also said that industry-wide pacing would require coordination between government and industry through a lawful, verifiable, and effective mechanism to guard against race-to-the-bottom dynamics. ([anthropic.com](https://www.anthropic.com/news/improving-alignment-security-efforts))
kept_facts.subject: Anthropic position on pacing frontier AI development
kept_facts.scope: Anthropic’s internal safety practices and proposed industry-wide coordination
kept_facts.conditions: The statement describes Anthropic’s position and does not establish that an industry-wide pacing mechanism exists.
kept_facts.source_title: Improving our alignment and security practices
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Use “Anthropic said” or equivalent attribution; do not state that the AI industry has agreed to slow development.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Anthropicは、社内でのフロンティア開発のペーシングを、安全と速度が衝突する場合に速度より安全を優先する判断と説明している。また、業界横断のペーシングには政府と産業界の調整、合法的・検証可能・有効な仕組みが必要で、race-to-the-bottomを防ぐ必要があると述べている。既存の業界合意があるとは主張していない。 ([anthropic.com](https://www.anthropic.com/news/improving-alignment-security-efforts?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash on 13 August 2026, three weeks after Gemini 3.6 Flash. Google said the newer model improved software-engineering, knowledge-work, and web-development workflows and shipped with updated safeguards for chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear misuse and cyber offense. ([blog.google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-3-7-flash/))
kept_facts.subject: Google Gemini model release cadence and safeguards
kept_facts.date_or_period: 13 August 2026; three-week interval from the prior Flash release
kept_facts.scope: Google’s Gemini Flash model line and associated product deployments
kept_facts.conditions: Capability and improvement descriptions are Google’s own product claims; safeguard availability may vary by product and use case.
kept_facts.numeric_scope: Release date and interval between Gemini 3.6 Flash and 3.7 Flash
kept_facts.source_title: Gemini 3.7 Flash: our most intelligent workhorse model
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: The short release interval documents deployment cadence; it does not by itself prove competitive pressure or a deliberate race motive.
kept_facts.verification_notes: GoogleはGemini 3.7 Flashを2026年8月13日に発表し、Gemini 3.6 Flashから3週間後のリリースだと説明している。ソフトウェア工学、知識労働、ウェブ開発の改善、およびCBRNとサイバー攻撃に対する更新済み安全策も、同社の発表に直接記載されている。改善性能はGoogle自身の製品主張として扱う必要がある。 ([blog.google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-3-7-flash/?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: Executive Order 14409, issued on 2 June 2026, stated that the United States would promote AI innovation and security while refusing to stifle innovation with overly burdensome regulation. The order also directed rapid deployment of secure AI capabilities and described the policy objective as enhancing U.S. national security and global AI dominance. ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/eo-14409.pdf))
kept_facts.subject: U.S. federal AI innovation and national-security policy
kept_facts.conditions: The order expresses executive-branch policy and directs federal actions; it is not itself a comprehensive federal AI regulatory statute.
kept_facts.source_title: Executive Order 14409 of June 2, 2026: Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Present this as the administration’s stated policy balance between innovation, security, and limited regulatory burden.
kept_facts.verification_notes: ホワイトハウスの公式文書は、2026年6月2日付のExecutive Order 14409として、AIイノベーションと安全の促進、過度に負担の大きい規制によるイノベーション阻害の回避、最も安全な技術の迅速な展開、米国の国家安全保障および世界的AI優位の強化を記載している。これは行政方針・行政措置であり、包括的な連邦AI規制法ではない。 ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/06/promoting-advanced-artificial-intelligence-innovation-and-security/?_bhlid=8f87c252690b4842c5f63c2563bebc40686efd8f&query-11-page=9&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block))

kept_facts.claim: On 3 September 2026, Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar announced forthcoming legislation that would permanently ban development and deployment of superintelligent AI and temporarily pause advanced AI development until a federal regulator establishes safety rules and a model-review process. The announcement also proposed international agreements to prevent superintelligence from being developed globally. ([sanders.senate.gov](https://www.sanders.senate.gov/press-releases/news-sanders-casar-introduce-legislation-to-ban-artificial-superintelligence-and-temporarily-pause-advanced-ai-development/))
kept_facts.subject: U.S. legislative proposal to pause advanced AI development
kept_facts.scope: Proposed U.S. federal legislation and proposed international policy
kept_facts.conditions: The measure was announced as forthcoming legislation; the source does not establish enactment into law.
kept_facts.source_title: Sanders, Casar to Introduce Legislation to Ban Artificial Superintelligence and Temporarily Pause Advanced AI Development
kept_facts.ambiguity: The proposal’s legislative status and prospects for passage are not established by the source.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Use “announced legislation” or “proposed bill,” not “U.S. law.”
kept_facts.verification_notes: Sanders議員とCasar議員が2026年9月3日に、Ban Artificial Superintelligence Actの提出予定を発表したことは確認できる。内容には超知能AIの開発・配備の恒久禁止、連邦規制機関が安全規則とモデル審査プロセスを整備するまでの先端AI開発停止、国際協定の追求が含まれる。成立・施行済みの法律ではない。 ([sanders.senate.gov](https://www.sanders.senate.gov/press-releases/news-sanders-casar-introduce-legislation-to-ban-artificial-superintelligence-and-temporarily-pause-advanced-ai-development/?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: Senator Mark Warner’s Secure AI Development Act, announced on 21 July 2026, would establish a mandatory secure testing environment for the United States’ most advanced AI models before deployment. The proposal would also modernize federal AI-cyber vulnerability disclosure and create a voluntary AI safety incident-reporting system. ([warner.senate.gov](https://www.warner.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/warner-rolls-out-comprehensive-ai-legislative-agenda-focused-on-responsible-innovation-workers-and-national-security/))
kept_facts.subject: U.S. congressional frontier-AI testing proposal
kept_facts.scope: Proposed federal requirements for the most advanced AI models and related federal reporting systems
kept_facts.conditions: The source describes proposed legislation; it does not establish enactment or implementation.
kept_facts.source_title: Warner Rolls Out Comprehensive AI Legislative Agenda Focused on Responsible Innovation, Workers, and National Security
kept_facts.ambiguity: The source does not establish whether the bill advanced, passed, or became law.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: This fact documents a legislative proposal for pre-deployment testing, not an operating federal testing regime.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Warner議員の2026年7月21日の発表は、Secure AI Development Actについて、最先端AIモデルの配備前の義務的な安全テスト環境、AIサイバー脆弱性の特定・開示手続の近代化、政府と開発者の情報共有、任意のAI安全インシデント報告制度を提案している。発表された立法提案であり、成立・実施済みの連邦制度ではない。 ([warner.senate.gov](https://www.warner.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/warner-rolls-out-comprehensive-ai-legislative-agenda-focused-on-responsible-innovation-workers-and-national-security/?utm_source=openai))
